rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise to strengthen Moses through his brother is metaphorical; God needs no aid, and calling them misleaders intensifies blame.
rows.anchor: أي سنعينك بأخيك. ولفظ العضد على جهة المثل، والله سبحانه وتعالى لا يحتاج إلى عون أحد.

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر الجحدري
rows.claim: He reads وما كنت with open second-person tāʾ, addressing Muhammad. The majority form of عضد is most eloquent, with seven other vocalic or dialect forms listed.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر الجحدري «وما كنت» بفتح التاء أي وما كنت يا محمد متخذ المضلين عضدا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call to summon partners is addressed to idolaters; they cannot answer or protect them. Hamza, Yahya, and Isa read نقول; the others say يقول, matching شركائي.
rows.anchor: أي اذكروا يوم يقول الله: أين شركائي؟ أي ادعوا الذين اشركتموهم بي فليمنعوكم من عذابي.

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك وابن عباس وابن الأعرابي
rows.claim: Mawbiq is a valley of pus and blood or a barrier between believers and unbelievers; another view puts it between idols and worshippers, while Ibn al-Arabi defines it as any separator.
rows.anchor: قال أنس بن مالك: هو واد في جهنم من قيح ودم.

rows.speaker: مجاهد ونوف البكالي وعكرمة وعطاء والضحاك وأبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Mujahid and Nauf say valley in Hell; Ikrima gives a fiery river and snakes; Ata and al-Dahhak say destruction, and Abu Ubayda an appointed destruction. The lexicon gives root forms.
rows.anchor: وذكر ابن وهب عن مجاهد في قوله تعالى: «موبقا» قال واد في جهنم يقال له موبق.

rows.speaker: الكوفيون وبعض البصريين ومحمد بن يزيد
rows.claim: Some write رأى with yāʾ; Muhammad ibn Yazid insists on alif and argues final weak verbs should be spelled alike whether their roots end in yāʾ or wāw.
rows.anchor: زعم الكوفيون أن «رأى» يكتب بالياء، وتابعهم على هذا القول بعض البصريين.

rows.speaker: author وابن عباس
rows.claim: ظنوا means certainty; Ibn Abbas says they knew they would meet the Fire. Another view says they thought it would seize them immediately; a report says an unbeliever expects it from forty years away. Alqama reads ملافوها, gathered in it.
rows.anchor: فظنوا» هنا بمعنى اليقين والعلم، كما قال:

rows.speaker: القتبي والفراء
rows.claim: Al-Qutabi glosses maṣrif as an avenue or refuge; al-Farra says worldly association becomes destruction in the afterlife. Muwāqaʿa means forceful contact.
rows.anchor: وقال القتبي: معدلا ينصرفون إليه. وقيل: ملجأ يلجأون إليه والمعنى واحد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran’s examples either recount instructive histories of past peoples as warning or clarify proofs of divine lordship as exposition.
rows.anchor: يحتمل وجهين: أحدهما: ما ذكره لهم من العبر والقرون الخالية.

rows.speaker: author والزجاج
rows.claim: The argumentative human is identified with al-Nadr ibn al-Harith or Ubayy ibn Khalaf; al-Zajjaj takes it as unbelievers generally. Anas reports an unbeliever’s limbs testifying at Judgment, and Ali reports the Prophet quoting the verse after a nighttime prayer exchange.
rows.anchor: والمراد به النضر بن الحارث وجداله في القرآن. وقيل: الآية في أبي بن خلف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance means Quran, Islam, and Muhammad; the exception refers to God’s practice of destroying earlier peoples and His decree, or their demand for that fate, as in 8:32.
rows.anchor: أي القرآن والإسلام ومحمد عليه الصلاة والسلام.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والكلبي ومقاتل
rows.claim: Punishment openly means visibly for Ibn Abbas, the sword at Badr for al-Kalbi, and suddenly for Muqatil. Readers explain قبلا as kinds, successive, all together, or visible punishment.
rows.anchor: ومعناه عيانا قاله ابن عباس. وقال الكلبي: هو السيف يوم بدر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Messengers promise Paradise to believers and warn unbelievers; false disputation is attributed to plotters calling Muhammad magician, madman, poet, or soothsayer. Idḥāḍ means invalidate and evokes slipping.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { وما نرسل المرسلين إلا مبشرين } أي بالجنة لمن آمن. { ومنذرين } أي مخوفين بالعذاب من كفر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mockery targets the Quran and its warnings; ما can mean warning itself or what was warned. Reports cite Abu Jahl’s Zaqqūm claim, Quran insults, objection to a human messenger, and demand for a notable recipient.
rows.anchor: { واتخذوا آياتي } يعني القرآن { وما أنذروا } من الوعيد { هزوا }.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worst wrongdoer rejects admonition; forgetting means leaving sins unrepented or forgetting deeds and punishment. Heart coverings and deafness result from disbelief; the verse concerns a group and rebuts Qadariyya.
rows.anchor: أي لا أحد أظلم لنفسه ممن وعظ بآيات ربه، فتهاون بها وأعرض عن قبولها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s forgiveness here is for believers in light of 4:48. ذو الرحمة can mean pardon, reward, blessing, or guidance; the last two extend to unbelievers. God delays punishment to a set term.
rows.anchor: وهذا يختص به أهل الإيمان دون الكفرة بدليل قوله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن زيد ومجاهد وقتادة وأبو عبيدة
rows.claim: The appointed term arrives in this life or the next; mawʾil is refuge, fortification, protector, deliverance, or escape. The author records lexical forms and poetry.
rows.anchor: أي ملجأ قاله ابن عباس وابن زيد، وحكاه الجوهري في الصحاح.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, تلك is subject and القرى its apposition or adjective; أهلكناهم is predicate. Another parse makes the villages accusative, referring to ʿĀd, Thamud, Midian, and Lot’s people. Readings vary on مهلكهم and it denotes their set time.
rows.anchor: «تلك» في موضع رفع بالابتداء. «القرى» نعت أو بدل.

rows.speaker: الجمهور ونوف البكالي
rows.claim: The majority identify Moses as Ibn Imran; Nauf posits Moses son of Manasha, a prophet before him, which Ibn Abbas rejects. The attendant is Joshua; لا أبرح means continue traveling or not part.
rows.anchor: الجمهور من العلماء وأهل التاريخ أنه موسى بن عمران المذكور في القرآن

rows.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد وابن عطية
rows.claim: They locate the confluence at the Persian and Roman seas; Ibn Atiyya describes an ocean arm through Persia. Other proposals include Jordan and Red Seas, Tangier, Africa, Armenia, and Andalusia; Moses and Khidr as the seas is rejected as weak.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: وهو بحر فارس والروم وقاله مجاهد.

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب وابن عباس
rows.claim: The Prophet says Moses claimed he was most learned, was reproached for not referring knowledge to God, and was sent to a more learned servant carrying a fish; Ibn Abbas gives a longer sermon account.
rows.anchor: إن موسى عليه السلام قام خطيبا في بني إسرائيل فسئل أي الناس أعلم فقال: أنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khidr’s greater knowledge concerns detailed rulings and cases, not absolute knowledge; each knew what the other did not. Moses eagerly sought knowledge, carrying salted fish in a basket.
rows.anchor: أي بأحكام وقائع مفصلة، وحكم نوازل معينة، لا مطلقا، بدليل قول الخضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥuqb is a long span, plural aḥqāb, sometimes eighty years or more. The story commends scholarly travel with a companion; Bukhari cites Jabir’s month-long journey for a hadith.
rows.anchor: بضم الحاء والقاف وهو الدهر، والجمع أحقاب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fata can mean a servant, a polite word for an attendant; Prophetic etiquette recommends it over my slave. Joshua is identified as Joseph’s descendant or Moses’ nephew, or a free learner accompanying Moses.
rows.anchor: قيل للخادم فتى على جهة حسن الأدب، وندبت الشريعة إلى ذلك في قول النبي

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: The Quran appears to make Joshua a slave, hadith identifies him as Joshua son of Nun, and tafsir calls him Moses’ nephew; none is certain, so suspension is safest.
rows.anchor: فظاهر القرآن يقتضي أنه عبد، وفي الحديث: أنه كان يوشع بن نون.

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو ومجاهد وقتادة والنحاس
rows.claim: Ḥuqb is variously eighty years, seventy autumns, or an indefinite period; standard Arabic leaves it unlimited and its plural is aḥqāb.
rows.anchor: قال عبد الله بن عمرو: الحقب ثمانون سنة.

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة وجمهور المفسرين
rows.claim: The dual refers to the seas and sarab to a path; Qatada says water froze. Most say the fish left an open track Moses followed to an island, though reports place Khidr on shore.
rows.anchor: الضمير في قوله: «بينهما» للبحرين قاله مجاهد. والسرب المسلك قاله مجاهد أيضا.

rows.speaker: author والبخاري
rows.claim: Only the attendant forgot to report the fish, but the lapse is attributed to both through companionship, like pearls from two seas and messengers from humans and jinn. Bukhari says Moses slept as it escaped and God held back the current.
rows.anchor: وإنما كان النسيان من الفتى وحده فقيل: المعنى نسي أن يعلم موسى بما رأى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view attributes neglect to both because they left the fish behind; nisyān can mean postponing. Moses felt fatigue only after passing the place. Provisioning is lawful and refutes ignorant Sufis.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن النسيان كان منهما لقوله تعالى: «نسيا» فنسب النسيان إليهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Bukhari report says Yemenis made pilgrimage without provisions and begged food; 2:197 commanded taking provisions.
rows.anchor: إن ناسا من أهل اليمن كانوا يحجون ولا يتزودون، ويقولون: نحن المتوكلون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو العباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the salted fish was food; Abu al-Abbas prefers it was only a sign for finding Khidr, so they carried other provisions. A preacher says Moses needed no food during communion but felt hunger walking to meet a human.
rows.anchor: كان حوتا مملوحا في زنبيل، وكانا يصيبان منه غداء وعشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naṣab means fatigue, perhaps hunger; reporting pain is permissible without undermining acceptance when done without resentment.
rows.anchor: والنصب التعب والمشقة. وقيل: عنى به هنا الجوع

rows.speaker: author وأبو شجاع وابن عطية
rows.claim: The Satan-forgetting phrase has a verbal clause as an inclusive substitute and a codex variant. Joshua apologizes. The fish’s route may be report or exclamation; it revived after death, and another parse makes it God’s report.
rows.anchor: وهذا إنما ذكره يوشع في معرض الاعتذار لقول موسى: لا أكلفك إلا أن تخبرني

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وسفيان
rows.claim: The fish revived after touching water from the spring of life; reports place it by the rock, and one tale says water from Moses’ beard revived it.
rows.anchor: أن الحوت إنما حيي لأنه مسه ماء عين هناك تدعى عين الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses says the lost fish was their sign and they retraced their steps. Bukhari describes finding Khidr on a green rug; al-Thaʿlabi gives a dialogue and a swallow taking water.
rows.anchor: أي قال موسى لفتاه أمر الحوت وفقده هو الذي كنا نطلب

rows.speaker: author ومجاهد
rows.claim: The servant is Khidr according to the majority and established reports; Mujahid says his surroundings turned green when he prayed.
rows.anchor: العبد هو الخضر عليه السلام في قول الجمهور، وبمقتضى الأحاديث الثابتة.

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A sound, rare Tirmidhi hadith says Khidr sat on a white furwa that turned green beneath him; furwa means the earth’s face.
rows.anchor: إنما سمي الخضر لأنه جلس على فروة بيضاء فإذا هي تهتز تحته خضراء

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority say Khidr was a prophet because hidden acts require revelation; other views call him righteous but not a prophet or an angel, but prophethood is preferred.
rows.anchor: والخضر نبي عند الجمهور. وقيل: هو عبد صالح غير نبي

rows.speaker: author وابن عطية
rows.claim: Mercy means prophethood or blessing; knowledge means the unseen. Ibn Atiyya contrasts Khidr’s revealed inward knowledge with Moses’ rulings from outward words and acts.
rows.anchor: الرحمة في هذه الآية النبوة. وقيل: النعمة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’ question is tactful and deferential; a learner follows a teacher without proving superiority. رشدا is the second object of teach.
rows.anchor: هذا سؤال الملاطف، والمخاطب المستنزل المبالغ في حسن الأدب

rows.speaker: author ومجاهد
rows.claim: Khidr says Moses cannot endure acts that seem wrong without knowing hidden wisdom; prophets cannot approve wrongdoing. خبرا is parsed as specification or a cognate accusative.
rows.anchor: لا تطيق أن تصبر على ما تراه من علمي لأن الظواهر التي هي علمك لا تعطيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses promises patience by God’s will and obedience; one view extends the exception to both clauses, while the other limits it to patience.
rows.anchor: أي سأصبر بمشيئة الله. { ولا أعصي لك أمرا } أي قد ألزمت نفسي طاعتك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view limits the exception to patience: Moses did question Khidr but did not qualify his resolve not to disobey. Scholars say future patience is uncertain or not acquired like obedience.
rows.anchor: وقيل: استثنى في الصبر فصبر، وما استثنى في قوله: { ولا أعصي لك أمرا } فاعترض وسأل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khidr’s condition that Moses not ask until he explains is discipline meant to preserve companionship; repeated objections made separation necessary.
rows.anchor: أي حتى أكون أنا الذي أفسره لك، وهذا من الخضر تأديب وإرشاد لما يقتضي دوام الصحبة

rows.speaker: البخاري ومسلم
rows.claim: The crew recognized Khidr and carried them without fare; Khidr pried off a plank with an adze, prompting Moses’ rebuke. The Prophet says Moses’ first objection was forgetfulness.
rows.anchor: فمرت سفينة فكلموهم أن يحملوهم، فعرفوا الخضر فحملوه بغير نول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A bird’s beakful illustrates human knowledge’s smallness beside God’s infinite knowledge; knowledge means known things and this is figurative, not a reduction.
rows.anchor: والعلم هنا بمعنى المعلوم، كما قال: ولا يحيطون بشيء من علمه

rows.speaker: أبو العالية وابن عباس
rows.claim: Only Moses saw Khidr pierce the boat, according to Abu al-Aliya; Ibn Abbas says Moses privately regretted leaving Israel and Khidr told him the thought. The incident supports protecting an orphan’s property.
rows.anchor: لم ير الخضر حين خرق السفينة غير موسى وكان عبدا لا تراه إلا عين من أراد الله

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: They read ليغرق with yāʾ and أهلها nominative as subject; the majority read لتغرق with a lām of outcome.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي «ليغرق» بالياء «أهلها» بالرفع فاعل يغرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza’s reading uses a purpose lām; Moses omits himself from the drowning accusation because compassion for the crew prevailed. Imran is glossed as astonishing, objectionable, or a great calamity.
rows.anchor: وعلى قراءة حمزة لام كي، ولم يقل لتغرقني لأن الذي غلب عليه في الحال فرط الشفقة عليهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He says Moses’ claim of forgetting is indirect speech; alternatively Moses truly forgot, showing involuntary forgetting brings no culpability or legal consequence.
rows.anchor: يروى عن ابن عباس، قال: هذا من معاريض الكلام.

rows.speaker: البخاري والصحيحان والترمذي
rows.claim: Reports say Khidr cut an unbelieving boy with a knife, pulled off his head, or crushed it with a stone; the author says these may have been sequential. Readings differ on زكية and its nuance.
rows.anchor: ولا اختلاف بين هذه الأحوال الثلاثة، فإنه يحتمل أن يكون دمغه أولا بالحجر

rows.speaker: الكلبي والجمهور
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says the boy was an adult bandit; the majority say he was not pubescent and would have led his parents to disbelief. Killing a child is allowed by God’s permission; a tale marks his bone as unbelieving.
rows.anchor: وقال الجمهور: لم يكن بالغا ولذلك قال موسى زاكية لم تذنب.

rows.speaker: ليلى الأخيلية وصفوان وابن عباس وابن جبير
rows.claim: Arguments for adulthood cite poems using ghulam of a young man, the boy’s criminality, Ibn Abbas’s highwayman view, and Ibn Jubayr’s legal-responsibility argument. Ghulam derives from intense desire.
rows.anchor: غلام إذا هوجيت لست بشاعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One group says nukran is stronger because killing is explicit while the boat’s danger was anticipated; another says imran is stronger because a group was at risk.
rows.anchor: فقالت فرقة: هذا قتل بين، وهناك مترقب ف«نكرا» أبلغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet usually began supplication with himself; he asks mercy for Moses and says patience would have shown wonders. ذمامة means scruple or shame about the companion after repeated objections.
rows.anchor: مسألة: أسند الطبري قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا دعا لأحد بدأ بنفسه

rows.speaker: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet wishes Moses had been patient long enough to tell their story.
rows.anchor: يرحم الله موسى لوددنا أنه صبر حتى يقص علينا من أمرهما

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب عن النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet calls the townspeople mean; they refuse hospitality, Khidr raises the leaning wall, and Moses suggests payment. The Prophet wished Moses had waited to hear the story.
rows.anchor: استطعما أهلها فأبوا أن يضيفوهما فوجدا فيها جدارا

rows.speaker: قتادة ومحمد بن سيرين والسهيلي والثعلبي
rows.claim: They propose Abulla, Antioch, Andalusia, Bagrowan, Berqa, or Nasira as the village; the disagreement reflects uncertainty about the journey’s location.
rows.anchor: فقيل: هي أبلة قاله قتادة، وكذلك قال محمد بن سيرين، وهي أبخل قرية

rows.speaker: author وقتادة
rows.claim: Moses was needier while watering Shuayb’s daughters but asked nothing; here food and hospitality are lawful to request and owed to travelers. The author rejects al-Hariri’s defense of persistent begging.
rows.anchor: كان موسى عليه السلام حين سقى لبنتي شعيب أحوج منه حين أتى القرية مع الخضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jidar and jadhr mean wall. The wall’s desire to collapse is figurative, glossed as leaning; the majority accept Quranic metaphor, while some reject it as implying divine inability.
rows.anchor: أي قرب أن يسقط، وهذا مجاز وتوسع وقد فسره في الحديث بقوله: «مائل»

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق الإسفراييني وأبو بكر محمد بن داود
rows.claim: They reject Quranic metaphor, arguing literal readings preserve truth and figurative speech would imply inability to speak literally, impossible for God.
rows.anchor: وذهب قوم إلى منع المجاز في القرآن، منهم أبو إسحاق الإسفراييني وأبو بكر محمد بن داود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verses and hadith about limbs, Hell, and objects speaking support literal speech because God can make creation speak; citations include 24:24, 50:30, 25:12, and 70:17.
rows.anchor: وما كان مثلها حقيقة، وأن خالقها الذي أنطق كل شيء أنطقها.

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك وأبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: Muslim says a person’s thigh, flesh, and bones testify at Judgment; Tirmidhi reports animals, a whip tip, sandal strap, and thigh will speak in this world and grades the report حسن غريب.
rows.anchor: فيختم على فيه ويقال لفخذه انطقي فتنطق فخذه ولحمه وعظامه بعمله

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الأنباري وسعيد بن جبير والثعلبي
rows.claim: A report has the Prophet read the wall as torn down then rebuilt, though the author prefers Said ibn Jubayr’s view that Khidr passed his hand over it; al-Thaʿlabi gives legendary dimensions.
rows.anchor: فوجدا فيها جدارا يريد أن ينقض فهدمه ثم قعد يبنيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khidr’s statement that he did not act on his own command indicates prophethood and revelation, though he was not a messenger.
rows.anchor: يدل على نبوته وأنه يوحى إليه بالتكاليف والأحكام، كما أوحي للأنبياء عليهم الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author وجرير
rows.claim: One should hurry past a dangerously leaning wall. Ṭirbāl means a high tower or wall fragment, with Jarir’s poetry cited. Saintly miracles are established by reports and scripture, including Mary’s seasonal fruit and Khidr’s acts.
rows.anchor: واجب على الإنسان ألا يتعرض للجلوس تحت جدار مائل يخاف سقوطه، بل يسرع في المشي

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء والجمهور
rows.claim: Some deny Khidr’s prophethood because solitary reports cannot establish it and no prophet follows Muhammad; the majority say he was a prophet without violating finality.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يقال كان نبيا لأن إثبات النبوة لا يجوز بأخبار الآحاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars differ whether saints may know their status. One view says no because signs may be a divine snare and destiny is hidden, so the saint must fear until angels descend, as in 41:30; al-Sari gives a bird-greeting example.
rows.anchor: ولأن الولي من كان مختوما له بالسعادة، والعواقب مستورة ولا يدري أحد ما يختم له به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opposing view permits knowledge: the Prophet knew his status and announced Paradise for ten Companions without ending their fear; Shibli’s assurance of protection was not a trap.
rows.anchor: القول الثاني: أنه يجوز للولي أن يعلم أنه ولي ألا ترى أن النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام يجوز أن يعلم
